cim: Orangeburg forum explores artificial intelligence, data centers
cim_eredeti: Orangeburg forum explores artificial intelligence, data centers
szoveg_eredeti:
ORANGEBURG, S.C. (WIS) - State Rep. Gilda Cobb-Hunter hosted a public education forum on artificial intelligence and data centers at Orangeburg-Calhoun Technical College.

The aim of the forum was to bring community members together to learn about the technology before making quick judgements.

“I suspect, like me, there are a lot of people who are using it that don’t really recognize it. The point tonight is to simply connect the dots, educate the community and be able to make informed decisions,” said Cobb-Hunter.

The forum followed Orangeburg County’s September approval of a moratorium halting new data center development and applications for at least 12 months. Elected officials, technology professionals and infrastructure representatives participated in the discussion.

Warren Harley, general manager of the city of Orangeburg’s Department of Public Utilities, said no plans are in motion for a data center at this time. He said any data center seeking to use the utility’s system would pay the cost of service rather than passing it on to customers.

“Whatever we do with respect to data centers or any big customer, that it doesn’t negatively impact our system or the customers we serve, from a rate perspective, from a cost perspective,” Harley said. “Any data center looking to come on to our system, whatever cost it is to serve, they will pay the cost and we will not pass that on to the customer.”

Orangeburg resident Rick Leonard said the discussion changed his thinking about the technology and its potential impact.

“I’m glad we’re taking a positive step, not just saying no and instead saying, ‘This might be a great thing and I don’t want us to miss the boat,’” Leonard said.

Cobb-Hunter said she is working to host a similar event in the near future.
